findings.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action calls current_user.id and tu.notification_level without any nil guard, so it crashes with NoMethodError when the request is anonymous or when no TopicUser row exists. Any recipient who is logged out (typical for email links) or who has never opened the topic gets a 500 from the unsubscribe URL in the email instead of the unsubscribe page; the GET-mutation also silently does nothing for anonymous users rather than prompting login.

[BUG] The rewritten unsubscribe_link locale now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only user_notifications.send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url, so every other email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true fails to render. I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) in message_builder.rb raises missing-interpolation-argument for digest/user mailer emails that set add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url, causing those email jobs to error and the mail to not be sent.

[BUG] unsubscribe_url builds on the relative url helper, producing a path like /t/slug/123/unsubscribe with no host, which is inserted verbatim into the email body markdown link. The 'click here' link in notification emails resolves against the recipient's mail client (no scheme/host), so clicking it opens a broken URL — the unsubscribe link is unusable in every email.

[BUG] topicUnsubscribe is registered as a top-level route, so the resolver looks for templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, but the diff creates the template at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is only found for a route nested in the topic resource. Visiting /t/slug/123/unsubscribe in the browser renders the route with no template — a blank page instead of the unsubscribe UI.

[ADVISORY] The route depends on PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id) as a static method on the PostStream model, which is not an established API in this codebase (existing code loads topic views via topic/model hooks and postStream.refresh). If the static loadTopicView class method does not exist, the unsubscribe route throws TypeError on entry and the page never renders; even if present, it bypasses the standard topic-loading path so preloading/errors behave inconsistently with the show route.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe state mutation is performed by a plain GET request with no CSRF token, no confirmation step, and no identity token in the URL (the emailed link is just /t/:id/unsubscribe authenticated only by the session cookie). Any page or email that embeds an image/link to /t/:id/unsubscribe silently changes the logged-in user's notification level for that topic, and the emailed link does not work for logged-out users at all; a per-user token in the URL (like the existing unsubscribe tokens) is required for a mail-driven unsubscribe.

[ADVISORY] The reworked template now emits the %{respond_instructions} footer both inside the context_posts block and again in the trailing footer, duplicating the respond instructions. Recipients of emails with context posts see the 'reply by email / visit link to respond' instructions twice in every notification email with previous discussion, which is a visible regression in the rendered mail.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the current_user has no TopicUser record for the topic, because TopicUser.find_by returns nil for a user who has never visited/tracked the topic but received the email via a mention or watched category. A recipient who never opened the topic clicks the unsubscribe link from the notification email, `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, and the request returns a 500 instead of unsubscribing the user — the feature's primary happy path fails for any user without a prior TopicUser row.

[BUG] The rewritten `unsubscribe_link` locale string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, so every call site that cooks I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', ...) without an unsubscribe_url template arg raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument. Any mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link without passing unsubscribe_url (user_notifications only adds it in send_notification_email at user_notifications.rb:295; any other builder user, e.g. digest-style or plugin mailers, and any unchanged spec constructing add_unsubscribe_link: true — the pre-existing spec neighbors in message_builder_spec.rb that were not updated) fails at Email::MessageBuilder#html_part with an exception instead of sending mail.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe endpoint mutates TopicUser.notification_level via an unauthenticated-token GET request, making it a state-changing GET that any logged-in user's browser can be tricked into issuing (CSRF via or link on any page). An attacker who posts or embeds a link to /t///unsubscribe silently mutes topics (or downgrades watching to regular) for every logged-in victim who loads the page — Discourse's CSRF protection does not cover GET routes.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe action's core behavior — the regular/muted toggle logic, the missing-TopicUser case, and the slug-mismatch 301 redirect — has no spec anywhere in this diff; the only test touched is message_builder_spec.rb's List-Unsubscribe header test. The next refactor of TopicUser change semantics (e.g. the nil-record crash at line 105, or a future signature change to TopicUser.change) will pass CI while breaking the email unsubscribe link for all users; the toggle regression is invisible until reported from production.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe action passes current_user into TopicView.new but performs the notification_level mutation without any explicit access check of its own, coupling unsubscribe authorization entirely to TopicView's access enforcement order. If TopicView defers its access check (it constructs lazily and the diff reads @topic_view.topic for the redirect before any check runs), a user who guesses/discovers a private-topic unsubscribe URL fetches topic metadata and mutates state on a topic they cannot read; verify the redirect-to-unsubscribe_url path cannot leak slug/title of restricted topics.

[ADVISORY] The client route creates a store record via this.store.createRecord('topic', { id: params.id }) then discards it on success (returning a different topic object), leaving an orphaned unsaved record in the identity map when the promise resolves with a fresh record. The next developer debugging Ember store warnings or extending this route inherits a leftover 'topic' record with the same id as the returned one, which will conflict with the identity map and make any later find/peek on that id return the stale created record's leftovers.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action mutates TopicUser.notification_level on a GET request with no confirmation step or CSRF-equivalent POST. Email scanners, link prefetchers, and browser previews (Gmail/Outlook fetch URLs) issue GETs on the unsubscribe URL embedded in every notification email, silently muting or downgrading the user's topic notification level without the user ever choosing to; the route map (config/routes.rb 'get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"') makes this reachable by any unauthenticated fetcher that obtains the emailed URL.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...) and then tu.notification_level without a nil guard on either current_user or tu. A recipient who follows the emailed unsubscribe link while logged out (no auth token exists in the link) hits current_user.id and gets a 500 NoMethodError instead of the unsubscribe page; likewise a user whose TopicUser row was never created for the topic crashes on tu.notification_level, returning 500 on a link the mailer just sent them.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe toggle mutes the topic when the user is already at regular level, so 'unsubscribe' has non-idempotent, escalating semantics not traceable to the stated intent of 'stop receiving notifications for this topic'. A user at regular (watching their own posts) who clicks the emailed link gets their topic fully muted rather than left at regular; a second click is a no-op state the UI never communicates, and the change is permanent with no undo prompt — the user is bitten immediately on first click of any email link.

[ADVISORY] This diff sweeps large amounts of unrelated style reformatting (hash-rocket to keyword hashes, brace style, whitespace, block shorthand) through topic_user.rb under the banner of the unsubscribe feature. The next maintainer doing git blame or a surgical revert of a topic_user.rb behavior must disentangle cosmetic churn from real changes; any bisect over this range returns a wall of formatting noise, making change-safety review of the actual feature harder.

[ADVISORY] The change to conditionally render the dropdown-button title (title becoming optional) is not traceable to any requirement of per-topic unsubscribe — it is drive-by scope expansion in a shared component. Every existing dropdown-button consumer now silently loses its title header if a future caller passes no title, and reviewers of this feature must audit a behavior change to a shared UI component whose blast radius is all dropdowns, not the unsubscribe page alone.

[ADVISORY] The wholesale re-indentation and restructuring of notification.html.erb is unrelated churn bundled into the unsubscribe feature; no requirement in the stated intent covers reformatting the email template. Anyone diffing future email-template regressions against this commit sees the entire file rewritten, obscuring which lines actually changed behavior and inflating the revert/bisect cost of the email rendering path, which is hard to test locally.

[ADVISORY] The html_part restructure moves the add_unsubscribe_link block inside the html_override guard, changing behavior for any builder invoked with add_unsubscribe_link but no html_override: previously the unsubscribe_link gsub ran (no-op) and now the whole block is skipped, and the trailing brace-style rewrite is unrelated to the feature. Any non-notification email that passes add_unsubscribe_link without html_override silently loses its unsubscribe-link substitution path after this restructure, and the reformat churn hides the control-flow change from reviewers scanning for feature code.

[ADVISORY] The per-topic unsubscribe sentence is unconditionally appended to the shared unsubscribe_link locale key used by every email that sets add_unsubscribe_link, regardless of whether that email type passed unsubscribe_url. Any mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link but not unsubscribe_url (e.g., digest, signup, system notifications) renders a broken '[click here](%{unsubscribe_url})' link or an I18n interpolation failure in its footer, exposing every email template to a regression caused by a locale string scoped for notification emails only.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately reads tu.notification_level, but find_by returns nil whenever the user has no TopicUser row for the topic. A user who receives a notification email for a topic they never opened in the app (TopicUser rows are created on visit, and notification emails are sent via TopicUser.change which only sets last_emailed_post_number on an existing row — but e.g. a newly created watcher row or edge paths can lack one) clicks the emailed /t/:id/unsubscribe link and gets NoMethodError on nil.notification_level → a 500 error page instead of the unsubscribe screen.

[BUG] The unsubscribe_link server locale now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url; any other mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url makes I18n raise MissingInterpolationArgument when html_part builds the unsubscribe link. Every HTML email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no unsubscribe_url opt (signup/activation/other user mailers reusing MessageBuilder with that flag) crashes during rendering, breaking those notification sends entirely.

[BUG] The email text promises 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' for both branches of the unsubscribe controller, but the controller demotes a tracking/watching user only to regular, which still delivers reply/mention notifications — the link's promise is only fulfilled for users already at regular (who get muted). A watching/tracking user who clicks the unsubscribe link continues receiving notification emails for that topic, contradicting the email copy and driving support complaints/repeated uninstalls; the state machine conflates two distinct intents (mute this topic vs. stop tracking) behind one unguarded toggle.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe action mutates persistent state (notification_level) on a plain GET request with no token, no guard clause, and a read-modify-write save (find_by → mutate → save!) rather than an atomic guarded update. The mutation is triggered by crawlers/prefetchers/link scanners following the emailed URL (email scanners routinely GET links), silently muting or demoting the user's notification level; the unguarded RMW also allows a lost update if the user changes level in the UI between the find and the save.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe raises for anonymous users: TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user) and current_user.id are dereferenced in an action added to skip_before_filter :check_xhr but with no visible login_required/current_user presence check in the diff. A logged-out user (or a user whose session expired) clicking the unsubscribe link from a mail client gets a 500 from TopicView/current_user.id rather than a sign-in redirect, so the feature is unusable for the exact audience the email reaches.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled stopNotificiationsText (extra 'i'), matched only by the equally misspelled template reference, and {{{...}}} renders it unescaped with the raw fancyTitle interpolated through a client.en.yml string containing <strong> markup. The typo-consistency between controller and template means any rename or new consumer of the correctly spelled name gets undefined; more concretely, the triple-stache renders model.fancyTitle-derived HTML — fancyTitle is server-sanitized so the immediate risk is contained, but the next editor adding a user-controlled field to that string inherits an XSS-shaped hole.

[ADVISORY] Adding render :show inside perform_show_response's format.html block changes the shared response path used by the show action, not just unsubscribe — previously the html format block only built preloaded data and the render happened implicitly via the view named after the calling action. The show action now explicitly renders the show template where it previously fell through to the default action-name render (also 'show', so behaviorally equivalent today), but if perform_show_response gains another caller (as this diff demonstrates it just did), the hardcoded render silently forces the show layout/template for that caller too — the unsubscribe HTML response is literally the full topic show page, not a dedicated unsubscribe view, coupling the two actions' HTML surfaces.

[BUG] The unsubscribe GET endpoint performs a state mutation with no confirmation and current_user is required, so an anonymous or logged-out recipient clicking the email link gets an auth error instead of unsubscribing. A user who clicks 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' from their email while not logged in (the common case for email links) is not unsubscribed and hits a login wall; the original intent — clicking the link stops notifications — silently fails.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the user has never interacted with the topic, and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError. A user who receives a notification email for a topic they haven't visited (e.g. via group mention or automatic tracking) clicks the unsubscribe link and gets a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page — the feature fails exactly on its target audience.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe URL acts as a toggle (tracking→regular, regular→muted) rather than a one-way unsubscribe, and for tracking users it sets 'regular' which still sends notifications. The email copy promises 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here', but a tracking user who clicks ends at 'regular' — still receiving every notification email; a second visit mutes instead. The implemented behavior silently drifted from the promised intent in server.en.yml.

[ADVISORY] The state-mutating notification-level change happens via GET on a URL embedded in emails, with no CSRF token or confirmation screen. Any party who obtains the URL (email scanners, link prefetchers, spam filters that follow links, anyone who guesses the topic id since there is no per-user token) silently changes the recipient's notification state without their consent; the intent of a per-topic unsubscribe was a user-controlled action, not a side-effecting GET.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe_url is unconditionally added for every notification email, so the unsubscribe_link locale block (which now contains both preference and per-topic lines) is rendered in all emails including digest/Signup/etc. contexts where a specific topic does not exist. Any mailer path using add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url interpolates an empty %{unsubscribe_url} into the per-topic line of every email, producing a broken '[click here]()' link in non-notification emails — the locale change made the old link text dependent on a new argument not universally supplied.

[ADVISORY] perform_show_response now unconditionally calls render :show in format.html, changing the HTML response of every topics#show request path that calls this method, not just unsubscribe. TopicsController#show (and now #unsubscribe) HTML responses render the show view with preloaded topic JSON; any existing show caller relying on the previous implicit render/redirect behavior (e.g. slug-mismatch flows) now double-renders or renders a full topic page where the unsubscribe intent was a lightweight confirmation page, and the unsubscribe HTML response shows the full topic UI rather than the intended minimal unsubscribe message.

[BUG] The `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's TopicUser notification_level via an unauthenticated-CSRF, state-changing HTTP GET with no CSRF token or origin check. An attacker embeds `` (or a link) in any page the victim views; when the victim is logged in, their browser issues the GET, `tu.save!` executes, and the victim's topic is silently muted — a textbook CSRF because GET-mutate is exempt from Rails' `protect_from_forgery` non-GET checks.

[BUG] `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil for any user who has never interacted with the topic, and the action calls `tu.notification_level` on nil. Any logged-in user clicking the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic they have no TopicUser row for gets a NoMethodError 500; the correct flow (create the row at :muted) is unreachable, and a 500-throwing GET mutator gives attackers a reliable crash-on-demand endpoint against any user.

[ADVISORY] `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders the I18n string with `model.fancyTitle` interpolated as raw HTML (triple-stache), and fancy_title is Discourse's cooked/HTML-bearing title format. The topic title's HTML is injected unescaped into the unsubscribe page; any sanitization gap or future change in fancy_title's allowlist (emoji/image markup) becomes stored XSS executed under the site's origin for any user who follows a per-topic unsubscribe link.

[ADVISORY] The per-topic unsubscribe URL embedded in every notification email contains no per-link token, relying entirely on the recipient's web session (current_user) for authorization. Users following the emailed link from a mail client where they are not logged in are bounced through login and land with no per-topic action completed (a design weakness vs. List-Unsubscribe token semantics), and the email URL itself cannot serve the RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe flow it advertises in headers.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe calls current_user.id and TopicUser.find_by(...) without nil checks, so any user without a TopicUser record for the topic gets a 500. An anonymous recipient clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link in the notification email, hits /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and current_user is nil → NoMethodError on current_user.id → 500 instead of a login redirect; likewise any logged-in user who never had a TopicUser row for that topic (created only via visits/track/reply) gets a 500 from tu.notification_level on nil tu. The entire unsubscribe feature's happy path in the email is the one path with zero tests in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The updated message_with_unsubscribe spec never asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe_url appears anywhere in the rendered email body, only that the List-Unsubscribe header is present. The new behavior in this diff — the unsubscribe_link locale text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} into the body via html_part's gsub — has no content assertion: if html_part drops the gsub, if MessageBuilder fails to pass unsubscribe_url into template_args, or if the mailer omits unsubscribe_url (user_notifications.rb:295 is the only producer and is untested), every test still passes because header_args['List-Unsubscribe'] presence is independent of body interpolation. I checked spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb (the only test file in the diff) — no expect touches body_part/html content or the unsubscribed URL string.

[ADVISORY] The core unsubscribe toggle semantics — level > regular → set regular, else set muted — is defined only in this controller and no spec in the diff (nor any referenced spec) exercises either branch. The mutation logic means a 'muted' user who clicks unsubscribe stays muted, and a tracking user is downgraded to regular (not muted) — counterintuitive behavior that users will report as 'the unsubscribe link didn't unsubscribe me' (clicking it while tracking still leaves them getting notifications for future posts, since regular still receives direct replies/mentions). Nothing in the diff pins down which level the link actually produces, so a future refactor flipping the comparison passes the suite silently. Checked spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb — the only test file touched — and no other spec files appear in the diff.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action calls tu.notification_level on the result of TopicUser.find_by without a nil check, so it raises NoMethodError whenever the logged-in user has no TopicUser record for the topic. A user who received the email (e.g. via a mention or reply that created a Notification but no TopicUser row for that user, or who opens the unsubscribe link while logged in as a different account) gets an unhandled 500 instead of the unsubscribe flow, and the notification level is not changed.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a state-destroying write (setting notification_level to muted) on a plain GET route with no CSRF-eligible method, no confirmation, and no key/token tying the link to the recipient, so any agent that fetches the URL mutes the topic. Email link-scanners and anti-virus/anti-spam gateways that prefetch GET links (a well-documented behavior) silently mute the topic for the recipient before they ever click, and the user cannot tell why notifications stopped; there is also no rollback for this silent state change — a prefetched mute is indistinguishable from a user-intended one.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe toggle is destructive-by-default in the wrong direction: a user at 'watching' who merely views the unsubscribe page (the GET action itself) is immediately flipped to 'regular' or 'muted' with no confirmation step. Any user who opens the link out of curiosity or to change their state loses their previous notification_level with no record of the prior value (no audit/backfill of the old level), so the previous preference is unrecoverable — clicking 'watching' again via the button on the page is the only restore path and the user must remember what they had.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the current_user has never had a TopicUser row for this topic, and the code immediately calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError. A user who receives a notification email for a topic they have never opened (e.g. mentioned on first post without visiting) clicks the emailed 'stop receiving notifications' link and gets a 500 error instead of the unsubscribe flow — the exact user-facing operation this feature exists for fails invisibly to logs-as-500.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action dereferences current_user.id with no anonymous-user guard, and no login-required before_filter covers this action. A logged-out user clicking the unsubscribe link in an email (very common — reading mail in a client without an active Discourse session) gets current_user as nil and a NoMethodError 500, instead of the standard redirect to the login page that all other user-scoped topic actions provide.

[BUG] The unsubscribe_link locale now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder only receives unsubscribe_url from send_notification_email; any other caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link (html_override present) without passing unsubscribe_url makes I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument in html_part. Any mailer besides the post-notification mailer that builds an HTML email with add_unsubscribe_link: true crashes at email render time, failing the whole notification send rather than degrading to a link-less footer.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe mutation (tu.notification_level = muted; tu.save!) is performed on an unauthenticated-safe plain GET request with no confirmation token and no logging. Mail-scanner/anti-virus link prefetch (Outlook SafeLinks, corporate gateways) hits the URL and silently mutes the topic for the user, who keeps receiving 'watching' expectations but no emails and no record anywhere that their state changed; there is also no audit trail distinguishing an intentional unsubscribe from a prefetch.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe action updates the TopicUser row with tu.save! directly, bypassing TopicUser.change, so the MessageBus '/topic/:id' notification_level_change publish that every other notification-level write emits is never sent. A user with the topic open in another browser tab unsubscribes via the email link and sees the notification-level button in the live tab still show 'Watching' — state desynced with no error surfaced, and the stale tab re-commits the old level if the user touches anything else on the topic.

[ADVISORY] The model hook's PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id) promise has no rejection handler and the route has no error action, unlike the sibling topic-from-params route which at least documents the failure. If loadTopicView 404s or the network fails after the server already mutated the notification level, the user gets Ember's unhandled-rejection 'oops' page with no indication that the unsubscribe actually succeeded or failed — a silently ambiguous user-facing outcome.

adjudication.rationale: `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is defined as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` (app/models/topic.rb), and elsewhere the diff indicates `post.url` is a relative path (email template uses `Discourse.base_url` + `post.url`), implying `topic.url` is also likely relative. That relative `unsubscribe_url` is passed into the email template args (user_notifications.rb) and interpolated into markdown `[click here](%{unsubscribe_url})` (server.en.yml) without prefixing `Discourse.base_url`, so the email body can contain a hostless link like `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe`, which is typically broken/useless in email clients expecting absolute URLs.

Visiting /t/slug/123/unsubscribe in the browser renders the route with no template — a blank page instead of the unsubscribe UI.

adjudication.rationale: The route map registers a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe` (`this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });`). The corresponding route/controller/view files are named `topic-unsubscribe` (e.g., `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`), which implies Ember will resolve the template `topic-unsubscribe`. However, the diff adds the template at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which would match a nested route like `topic.unsubscribe`, not `topicUnsubscribe`. No `templateName` override is shown, so this mismatch would result in the route rendering without the intended template (blank/missing UI).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The route depends on PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id) as a static method on the PostStream model, which is not an established API in this codebase (existing code loads topic views via topic/model hooks and postStream.refresh). Because it’s a GET with no CSRF-protected method and no per-recipient/token parameter, any authenticated fetch of the URL (e.g., link prefetchers, previews, or CSRF via an `` while the user is logged in) can silently change notification state without explicit user intent or confirmation.
